title: DECLARE PSALM 145 AND PRAISE GOD IN THE MORNING
text: Hallelujah. Hallelujah. Give the Lord a hand of praise right where you are. Come on, lift your hands and worship him. Father, we give you glory. We give you honor. We bless your name. You are worthy, Lord. You are worthy of all praise. You were before time began and you will remain when time is [music] no more. Father, we receive your word this morning. Let your spirit move. In Jesus' name we pray. Amen. I want you to be seated. And I want to talk to you this morning about something that is going to change the spiritual climate of your life permanently. I want to talk to you about the power of beginning your morning with a declaration. Not just any declaration, not a motivational quote, not a self-help affirmation, but a divinely inspired, spirit-breathed, covenant-backed declaration from the word of the living God. Specifically this morning, I want to talk to you about Psalm 145. Before we go in, understand this. The enemy does not fear how much money you have. The enemy does not lose sleep over your education or your social influence. But there is something that terrifies principalities and powers. It is a believer who understands their covenant rights and opens their mouth every single morning with the word of God. When you declare Psalm 145 inches the morning, you are not doing a religious ritual. You are engaging cosmic forces. You are rewriting the spiritual narrative of your day before the day even begins. You are establishing jurisdiction. You are setting the terms and conditions of what can and cannot happen in your life, your family, your career, your health, your destiny. There is something about the morning that the scriptures treat with unusual reverence. David said in Psalm 5:3, "My voice shall thou hear in the morning, O Lord. In the morning will I direct my prayer unto thee and will look up." Lamentations 3:23 says that his mercies are new every morning, not [music] every afternoon, not every evening, every morning. There is a fresh allotment of divine mercy, divine favor, divine grace, divine provision that is released at the threshold of every morning. The question is not whether those blessings are available. The question is whether you position yourself spiritually to receive and activate them. And one of the most powerful ways to do that is to [music] open your mouth and declare the word of God over life before anything else has a chance to speak. Before the news speaks to you, you speak the word. Before your fears speak to you, you speak the word. Before your circumstances speak to you, you speak the word. Before the enemy gets a chance to set the agenda for your day, you establish the agenda with the breath of the almighty. This is not a concept I want you to merely agree with intellectually. This is a lifestyle I'm inviting you into, a daily spiritual discipline that the greatest warriors in scripture practice consistently. Job said in Job 1:5 that he rose up early in the morning and offered burnt offerings. Moses met with God in the morning on the mountain. Abraham rose up early in the morning in Genesis 22 to obey God. Jesus himself, in Mark 1:35, "Rising up a great while before day, departed into a solitary place and there prayed." The son of God, the one who had all power and all authority, still saw it fit to begin his day in the presence of the Father. If Jesus needed a morning encounter, how much more do we? Now, Psalm 145 is not just any Psalm. It is the only Psalm specifically described in Hebrew tradition as a Tehillah, a praise of David. It is an acrostic Psalm in the original Hebrew, meaning every verse begins with a successive letter of the Hebrew alphabet from aleph to tav, the equivalent of alpha to omega, a way of saying that the praise of God is complete and comprehensive. It covers everything from beginning to end. There is nothing outside the praise of God. There is no territory, no domain, no dimension of human existence exempt from the sovereignty, the goodness, and the faithfulness of the God we serve. Listen to how David begins. Verse one. I will extol thee, my God, O king, and I will bless thy name forever and [music] ever. Before David asks God for anything, before he presents a petition, before he lists his needs, he makes a decision. He says, "I will." That is a volitional declaration, a determination of the will. He's not saying, "I feel like it this morning." He's not making his worship conditional on his emotional [music] state. He makes a sovereign decision. I will extol thee. I will bless thy name. This is a fundamental principle of spiritual warfare that most believers have not learned. You cannot afford to wait until you feel like praising God before you praise God. Because if you wait until you feel like it, the enemy will make sure you never feel like it. Praise is not first an emotional response. Praise is first a decision. Psalm 22:2-3 says, "He inhabits the praises of Israel." The Hebrew word is yashab, which means [music] to sit down, to settle, to dwell, to make one's home in. God does not just visit praise. He settles in praise. He makes his throne [music] in praise. Which means when you begin your morning with genuine, deliberate, scripture-based [music] praise, you are literally constructing a throne for the King of kings in your life. And when God is enthroned in your situation, every enemy bows, every mountain dissolves, every obstacle loses its power. Verse three says, "Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised and his greatness is unsearchable." The word unsearchable in the Hebrew is checker, which means beyond investigation, beyond comprehension, beyond the reach of human inquiry. You cannot bottom out the greatness [music] of God. You cannot exhaust his wisdom. You cannot calculate the full measure of his goodness. And when you understand that the God you are declaring in the morning is unsearchably great, it destroys [music] every form of doubt. It dismantles every logic that says your problem is too big. If you cannot find the limit of his greatness, then you cannot justify the conclusion that his greatness is insufficient for your situation. If his greatness is unsearchable, there is no bottom to what he can do. There is no ceiling to how high he can take you. There is no situation too complex, [music] too tangled, too far gone that he cannot unravel and resolve. And you are in covenant with this God. You carry his name. You are sealed with his spirit. You are washed in his blood. And this is the God you are declaring at the break of day. Verse eight says, "The Lord is gracious and full of compassion, slow to anger and of great mercy." This is a declaration about the character of God. And this is extremely important because the enemy's primary strategy is to corrupt your image of God. If he can convince you that God is harsh, that God is disappointed in you, that God is withholding from you, he can paralyze your faith and disconnect you from your spiritual inheritance. But when you declare Psalm 145 in the morning, [music] you are recalibrating your revelation of God. He is gracious. He is full of compassion. He is slow to anger. He is of great mercy, not limited mercy. Not occasional mercy. Great mercy. And when this becomes the lens through which you see God every morning, it liberates your faith. I want to talk to somebody who has been struggling to pray. Somebody who has been struggling to come to God because of guilt, because of past mistakes, because of a sense of unworthiness. This Psalm is medicine for you this morning. The Lord is gracious, he is full of compassion, his anger is slow, his mercy is great, he has not rejected you, he has not turned his face from you. He is waiting with open arms to receive you, to restore you, to refresh you, to renew you. And I need you to hear this clearly, your past does not have the final word over your future. The enemy is a revisionist historian. He loves to replay your failures on the screen of your memory to convince you that your history disqualifies you from your destiny, [music] but God is not moved by your history. God is moved by your faith. And Hebrews 11 tells us that by faith, by faith, by faith, ordinary people with extraordinary failures did extraordinary things because they dared to believe that God's mercy was greater than their mistakes. Verse 14 says, "The Lord upholdeth all that fall, and raiseth up all those that be bowed down." Someone is listening right now, and you are fallen. Not necessarily spiritually, but in your business, your marriage, your health, your finances, and there is a voice telling you that you cannot get back up. But the word says, "The Lord upholdeth all that fall." Not some that fall, all. "He also raiseth up all those that be bowed down." If you are bowed down this morning under the weight of grief, disappointment, or failure, God says he is your raiser, he is the lifter of your head. Psalm 3:3. He is reaching down right now to restore your dignity, reestablish your purpose, and revive your destiny. Verses 15 and 16. "The eyes of all wait upon thee, and thou givest them their meat in due season. Thou openest thine hand, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing. God opens his hand, not reluctantly, not with hesitation. He opens his hand freely, generously, graciously. And what comes from the open hand of God? Satisfaction. Not partial satisfaction. He satisfies the desire of every living [music] thing. Philippians 4:19 says, "My God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus." Not according to your current salary, not according to your present circumstances. According to his riches in glory. When you declare Psalm 145, you are accessing the open hand of God. You are positioning yourself under the overflow of divine provision. Verse 18 says, "The Lord is nigh unto all them that call upon him, to all that call upon him [music] in truth." The almighty God, the creator of the heavens and the earth, the one whose greatness is unsearchable, is near to everyone who calls upon him in truth. The only condition is sincerity, genuine, authentic, heart-level calling upon God. And the promise is stunning. He is near, he is close, he is accessible. He is not on the far side of the universe, indifferent to your cry. Psalm 46:1 says, "God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble." Very present, not occasionally present. Very present in trouble. I want to pause here and speak to the person who has been praying and feels like heaven is silent. You have been faithful, you have been declaring, you have been showing up in the morning. And yet the answer has not come in the form you expected. And there is a temptation to conclude that God is not near. That your prayers are bouncing off the ceiling, that you are speaking into empty air. But I need you to hear what the spirit is saying. Divine nearness is not always demonstrated through immediate answers. Sometimes God's nearness is demonstrated through supernatural peace in the middle of an unanswered prayer. Philippians 4:2-7 says, "The peace of God that passes all understanding shall guard your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus." That peace that you cannot explain, that calm that does not make sense given your circumstances, that steadiness that your friends marvel at, that is the evidence of his nearness. He is near. He has always been near, and the answer is being prepared even now in the chambers of heaven. Now, I want us to pray. And I need this to be a real prayer, not a religious performance, a genuine militant faith-filled conversation with the living God, saturated in the declarations of Psalm 145. Understand that prayer is not informing God of things he does not know. Prayer is alignment, prayer is agreement, prayer is the human spirit engaging with divine purposes and releasing them into earthly manifestation. Matthew 6:10, "Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven." Implies that what is in heaven is not automatically in earth. Something must happen in earth for heavenly realities to manifest, and that something is prayer. Before we go into prayer, I want to encourage you to share this ministration. Do not keep it to yourself. The person who needs this word is waiting for you to send it. That friend who wakes up every morning drowning in anxiety before the day even begins, that family member who has lost hope, that colleague who does not know the power of beginning the day in God's presence, they need this. Proverbs 11:25 says, "He that watereth shall be watered also himself." When you share this word, you are sowing a seed that returns to you multiplied. Forward it, post it, send it. Be a carrier of this grace. Lift your hands wherever you are. Open your mouth. Father, in the name of Jesus Christ, the name above every name, the name at which every knee shall bow, we come into your presence this morning. We come not with our own righteousness, but through the blood of Jesus Christ, [music] through the finished work of Calvary, through the resurrection power that raised Christ from the dead and seated him at the right hand of the Father far above all principality and power. We come in that name. We come through that covenant. Father, we extol you this morning. We declare with the words of Psalm 145 that you are great and greatly to be praised. Your greatness is unsearchable. There is no limit to your power. There is no bottom to your wisdom. There is no end to your goodness. [music] You are El Shaddai, God almighty, the God of more than enough. You are Jehovah Jireh, the God who sees and provides. You are Jehovah Rapha, the God who heals every sickness and disease. You are Jehovah Nissi, our victory in every battle. You are Jehovah Shammah, the Lord who is present, who has never left and will never leave. We extol you. We magnify your name. You alone are worthy. You alone are holy. You alone are God. Father, we declare that your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom. We declare that every counterfeit kingdom, every fake authority, every illegitimate power [music] operating in our lives and in our territories is exposed this morning. It is dismantled. It is dethroned by the authority of the everlasting kingdom of God, by the blood of Jesus Christ. We say to every throne erected contrary to your will, "Come down in the name of Jesus." Every stronghold established over our destinies, we command it to crumble because the kingdom of God is here. And before the king, every counterfeit must bow. Father, we declare that you are gracious and full of compassion. We receive your grace this morning. Father, there are people praying right now who have been disqualified by guilt, who have been carrying the weight of past mistakes, convinced they are too far gone for your mercy. Let your compassion speak louder than their guilt. Let your grace speak louder than their shame. For the word says, "If we confess our sins, you are faithful and just to forgive us and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. All, not some. All." Let the cleansing power of the blood of Jesus touch every life listening right now. Wash them, Father. Renew them. Restore them. Reinstate them. Father, we declare that you open your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing. We receive our provision in due season. We declare that lack does not have [music] a home in our lives. Shortage does not have jurisdiction in our households. Poverty is not our portion because our God opens his hand over us. Father, every financial door that has been shut, [music] open it now in the name of Jesus. Every supply line the enemy has blocked, unblock it. Every blessing withheld, we call it forth. Every inheritance stolen, we demand its return with sevenfold increase according to Proverbs 6:31. Let provision flow. Let abundance come. Let prosperity manifest. Not for the love of money, but for the advancement of your kingdom and for the testimony of your goodness. Now, this is warfare prayer. This is not asking prayer. This is declaring, commanding, enforcing prayer. The prayer of a believer who knows their authority. Because Colossians 2:15 says, "He spoiled principalities and powers. He made a show of them openly. He triumphed over them in the cross." Past tense. Done. Finished. You are not fighting for victory, you are fighting from victory. You are not trying to defeat the enemy, you are enforcing the enemy's [music] already accomplished defeat. I declare that divine preservation is activated over my life. Every accident arranged against me, I cancel it. Every ambush, every trap, every snare of the fowler, I cancel [music] it. Psalm 91 says, "A thousand shall fall at thy side and 10,000 at thy right hand, but [music] it shall not come nigh thee." I declare this over my life today, over my family today. I am under divine preservation. I am covered by the wings of the Almighty. I am shielded by the blood of Jesus. And no weapon, no plan, no scheme formed against me shall prosper because I am preserved by the God who never sleeps. Father, in the name of Jesus, I come against every spiritual force of wickedness that has established itself against the destinies of your people. By the blood of the lamb and by the word of our testimony, we overcome. Revelation 12:11. We apply the blood of Jesus over our lives, our families, our homes, our places of work, our finances, our health, our minds. The blood of Jesus speaks on our behalf, speaking better things than the blood of Abel. Mercy, redemption, restoration, deliverance, protection. [music] I declare that sickness has no legal right in my body. I am the temple of the Holy Spirit. [music] 1 Corinthians 6:19. And I command every sickness, every disease, every infirmity, every pain in my body or in the bodies of those I'm praying for leave in the name of Jesus, by the stripes of Jesus. 1 Peter 2:24 says, "By whose [music] stripes you were healed." Were healed, past tense. The healing is done. The healing is paid for. Let healing manifest now. Let bodies be restored. Let organs function properly. [music] Let tumors dissolve. Let depression lift. Let anxiety flee. Let mental clarity come. For the same spirit that raised Christ from the dead dwells in you, and he shall quicken your mortal bodies. Romans 8:11. Father, I speak to barren wombs this morning. Your covenant includes fruitfulness. Exodus 23:26 says, "There shall nothing cast their young, nor be barren in thy land." To every man and woman waiting for the fruit of the womb, who has been told by doctors it is not possible, who has cried in the night season, I declare that he who gave Sarah a child past the age of natural possibility, who opened Rachel's womb, who gave Hannah her Samuel, that same God is speaking to your situation right now. At this season you shall embrace. In Jesus' name, receive it. Father, I declare that the spirit of depression is broken. Every spirit of hopelessness is broken. Every spirit of despair is broken. The spirit of heaviness is commanded to go, and the garment of praise comes in its place. Isaiah 61:1-3, "The oil of joy for mourning." Because you are a tree of righteousness, planted by the rivers of water, and you shall bring forth fruit in your season. I want to speak to the person whose mind has been a battlefield. The person who wakes up, and the first thing that greets them is a torrent of anxious thoughts. Thoughts about tomorrow. Thoughts about money. Thoughts about what people think. Thoughts about what might go wrong. I want you to know that 2 Corinthians 10:2-4 and 5 says, "The weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds." Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalted itself against the knowledge of God, bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ, you have authority over your thought life. You do not have to accept every thought the enemy deposits in your mind. When you begin your morning with Psalm 145, you are literally evicting the toxic thoughts and replacing them with the thoughts of God. Isaiah 55:8 says, "His thoughts are not your thoughts. His thoughts toward you are thoughts of peace and not of evil." Jeremiah 29:11 thoughts to give you a future and a hope. Flood your mind with these thoughts every morning and watch the battlefield of your mind become a sanctuary of peace. I prophetically declare that the season of fruitlessness is over. The season of labor without result is ending. [music] What is beginning is a season of supernatural harvest. A season where you will work and it will produce. A season where you will plant and it will bear fruit. Amos 9:13 says, "The days come that the plowman shall overtake the reaper." The harvest will be so great [music] that before you finish reaping, it will already be time to sow again. This is your season. [music] Receive it in the name of Jesus. I prophetically declare that divine speed is coming upon your life. What took others 20 years, God is going to accomplish in your life in two. What the enemy stole from previous seasons, God is going to restore with supernatural speed. Joel 2:25 says, "I will restore to you the years that the locusts have eaten." Restoration with divine speed. Restoration that leaves people asking, "How did this happen so quickly?" And the answer will be simple, "God did it." Father, I want to pray a final prayer over everyone who has engaged with this ministration. I thank you for every person who gave you the first moments of their day. Who chose to declare your name before the noise of the world could fill their spirit. Father, reward their faithfulness. For you have said those who seek you shall find you. You are a rewarder of them that diligently seek you. Hebrews 11:6. Let them see the difference today. Let signs follow. Let breakthroughs manifest. Let doors open. Let provision come. Let healing begin. Let peace surpass understanding. Let joy arise. Let faith be strengthened. Father, I pray for every marriage under attack. I declare that what God has joined together no devil can put asunder. Peace in homes this morning. Love rekindled. Forgiveness released. Unity reestablished. In Jesus' name. Father, every young person at a crossroads trying to find their purpose, let your voice be clear to them. Isaiah 30:21 says you shall hear a voice behind you saying, "This is the way. Walk ye in it." Let that voice speak clearly today. And Father, for every minister of the gospel, every pastor, every intercessor, every worship leader who is weary and considering giving up, I speak to you by the spirit of God. Do not faint. Do not throw away your confidence. Galatians 6:29 says, "In due season you shall reap if you faint not." [music] Your due season is approaching. Your latter end shall be greater than your beginning. The best of what God has for you has not yet come. Hold on. Keep declaring. Keep showing up. Keep opening your mouth in the morning. For your morning of weeping is giving way to a morning of joy. Psalm 30:5. >> [music] >> Weeping may endure for a night, but joy cometh in the morning. And to every power that has been opposing the progress of these precious saints, I speak with the authority of the name of Jesus. Your assignment is terminated. Your jurisdiction is revoked. Your access is denied. The blood of Jesus is against you. The word of God is against you. The angels of God are against you. And if God be for us, who can be against us? Romans 8:31. Let every opponent bow. Let every obstacle fall. Let the victory of the Lord be manifest. I release a prophetic blessing over your life right now. Over your morning, over your day, over your season, over your generation. The blessing of Abraham comes upon you. The blessing of Isaac that went in the same year a hundredfold comes upon you. The blessing of the new covenant sealed with the blood of Jesus, [music] purchased by his death, ratified by his resurrection, administered by his Holy Spirit comes upon you in full measure. Pressed down, shaken together, and running over. Luke 6:38. And I declare that from this day forward your mornings will never be the same. You will open your mouth every morning before the world speaks and you will speak first. [music] You will declare the character of your God. You will release his word over your life. And you will watch as the God of Psalm 145 shows up in ways that make testimony inevitable. In ways that make people look at your life and say, "Surely the Lord has been good to this person." Surely the tender mercies of God are over this person's life. Say amen. Not as a ritual word, as a declaration of agreement. Amen means so be it. Let it come to pass. [music] Let it manifest in earth as it is in heaven. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, the love of God, the fellowship of the Holy Ghost be with you and with every person connected to your [music] life. The blessing of the Lord it maketh rich and he added no sorrow with it. This is your word. This is your portion. This is your inheritance. Walk in it. Declare it. Live it. And let the God of Psalm 145 be glorified in your life from this morning into eternity [music] in Jesus mighty name. Amen. Amen. Amen. Hallelujah.
